answer: To resist sybil attacks in an AI-agent economy, each identity must periodically submit a unique verifiable simulation of copper ion diffusion across a lagoon whose boundary is defined by a shifting coastal dune. The model uses a private seed from the agent key and must match public tide and salinity data within tight bounds. An attacker cannot reuse one solve: every fake identity demands its own high-fidelity physics run, so the cost scales linearly with fleet size in compute and data validation effort while honest agents pay only for their single ongoing model.
